name: Brazilian Chickpea Curry over Roasted Spaghetti Squash with Cilantro

instructions.primary_message: Preheat the oven to 260°C (500°F) and place the rack in the center position. Line two baking sheet pans with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 medium spaghetti squash
3 green bell peppers
1 small bunch cilantro
1 ½ limes

instructions.primary_message: Trim off and discard ends of each squash; halve squash lengthwise and scrape out the seeds from each half. Rub the inside of the squash with oil and season with salt and pepper. Arrange the squash halves cut-side-down on the baking sheets.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, 25-30 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse the chickpeas; transfer to a large pot.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell peppers; add to the pot with the chickpeas.
Add tomatoes, coconut milk, and spices to the pot; stir to combine the curry and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 (398 ml) cans diced tomatoes
1 ½ (398 ml) cans coconut milk
2 tbsp paprika
2 tbsp cumin, ground
1 tbsp brown sugar
1 ½ tsp garlic powder
1 ½ tsp onion powder
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp cayenne pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the curry is boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Cut limes into wedges and set aside.

Remove squash from the oven; allow to cool slightly, about 5 minutes. Scrape the inside of the squash with a fork to separate into spaghetti-like strands. (Use an oven mitt or towel to hold it with your other hand.)
To serve, divide squash and curry between plates; top with cilantro, yogurt, and a squeeze of lime. Enjoy!
